pass_a_gloss: Joshua 24 as catechumenal covenant; denial as truce-breaking and Satan re-embraced; Eli's unanswerable sin.
pass_b_english: What Jesus said, then, settling the people on the holy land, Scripture might now say to us. The wording runs: 'Now fear the Lord, and serve him in uprightness and righteousness.' (Joshua 24:14–18) And to us, persuaded to commit idolatry, it will say this and what follows, running thus: 'Put away the strange gods your fathers served beyond the river and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.' (1 Samuel 2:25) At the beginning, when you were about to be catechized, it would rightly have been said to you: 'But if it please you not to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves this day whom you shall serve — whether the gods of your fathers beyond the river, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.' And your catechist would have said to you, 'But I and my house shall serve the Lord, for he is holy.' Now these have no place being said to you. For then you said, 'Far be it from us to forsake the Lord to serve other gods. The Lord our God himself is God, who brought us and our fathers up from Egypt, and kept us in all the way we walked in.' But in the godliness compacts too, you answered your catechists of old with this: 'We too shall serve the Lord; for this is our God.' If, then, he who transgresses compacts with men is a truce-breaker, foreign to salvation — what of those who, by denying, annul the compacts they made with God, running back to Satan, whom at baptism they renounced? To such must be said the words Eli spoke to his sons: 'If a man sinning sin against a man, they shall pray for him; but if he sin against the Lord, who shall pray for him?'
